meals.name: Breakfast: Moong Dal Chilla with Mint Chutney & Curd
meals.reason: High-protein vegetarian breakfast rich in bioavailable plant protein, iron, and gut-friendly probiotics.
instructions: Soak split yellow moong dal for 30 mins, then grind into a smooth batter with ginger and green chillies.
Heat a non-stick pan with minimal oil spray and spread a ladle of batter thinly.
Sprinkle crumbled paneer and fresh coriander on top, flip gently, and cook both sides until golden brown.
Serve warm with fresh mint-coriander chutney and 1 cup of curd.

meals.name: Lunch: Paneer Tikka with Yellow Tadka Dal & Brown Rice
meals.reason: Complete amino acid profile pairing legumes with brown rice, balanced with high-calcium dairy.
instructions: Marinate paneer cubes with curd, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, and lemon juice for 15 mins.
Grill paneer on a skillet or air fryer for 8 mins until charred at the edges.
Serve with freshly prepared yellow dal tadka, steamed brown rice, and fresh lemon kachumber.

meals.name: Dinner: Palak Paneer with Whole Wheat Phulkas & Salad
meals.reason: Rich in lutein, iron, and magnesium to promote restful sleep and night muscle synthesis.
instructions: Blanch washed spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 mins, then plunge into cold water and blend with green chilli.
Sauté garlic, cumin seeds, and chopped onion in 1 tsp ghee, then pour in spinach purée.
Stir in soft paneer cubes and a pinch of garam masala. Simmer on low heat for 4 mins.
Serve warm with hot oil-free phulkas.

meals.name: Snack: Sprouted Moong Chaat with Pomegranate & Lemon
meals.reason: Low glycemic load, high dietary fiber, and active digestive enzymes.
instructions: Toss sprouted moong with diced onions, tomatoes, green chillies, and sweet pomegranate pearls.
Season with black salt, roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and fresh lemon juice.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.

meals.name: Breakfast: Vegetable Oats Upma with Peanuts & Boiled Sprouts
ingredients: 1/2 cup mixed diced veggies (carrots, peas, beans)
1 tsp mustard seeds and curry leaves
meals.reason: High in beta-glucan fiber for cholesterol control and sustained glycemic release.
instructions: Dry roast rolled oats in a skillet for 3 mins until fragrant.
Splutter mustard seeds, green chilli, and curry leaves in 1 tsp olive oil or ghee.
Sauté diced vegetables and boiled sprouts until tender-crisp.
Add 2 cups of hot water and roasted oats, simmering for 4 minutes until thick and fluffy.

meals.name: Lunch: High-Protein Rajma Masala with Quinoa & Steamed Beans
meals.reason: Dense in plant protein, dietary fiber, magnesium, and resistant starch.
instructions: Pressure cook soaked rajma with aromatics (onion, ginger-garlic, tomato purée, and garam masala).
Simmer rajma until the gravy is rich and velvety.
Serve over fluffy cooked quinoa with lightly spiced cucumber raita and steamed vegetables.

meals.name: Dinner: Moong Dal Khichdi with Roasted Papad, Curd & Baingan Bharta
ingredients: 1.25 cups moong dal & brown rice khichdi
meals.reason: Light, highly digestible dinner promoting gut restoration and optimal recovery.
instructions: Combine equal parts yellow moong dal and rice with turmeric, cumin, and salt in a cooker.
Roast eggplant over an open flame, peel, mash, and sauté with onions and tomatoes.
Serve steaming khichdi with a dash of pure ghee, spiced baingan bharta, and curd.

meals.name: Snack: Roasted Makhana (Fox Nuts) & Handful of Almonds
meals.reason: Rich in magnesium and antioxidants, perfect for satisfying crunch without extra calories.
instructions: Dry roast makhana in a heavy pan on low heat with a pinch of turmeric, black pepper, and rock salt until crunchy.
Pair with raw almonds and a hot cup of unsweetened green tea.

meals.name: Breakfast: Paneer Stuffed Multigrain Paratha with Curd
meals.reason: Wholesome complex carbohydrates paired with slow-digesting casein protein.
instructions: Mix grated paneer with chopped green chillies, coriander, cumin powder, and a pinch of salt.
Stuff into whole wheat or multigrain dough and roll out smoothly.
Cook on a medium hot tawa with a light brush of ghee until crisp.
Enjoy with probiotic plain curd and cooling cucumber slices.

meals.name: Lunch: Soya Chunk Matar Curry with Multigrain Rotis & Curd
meals.reason: Massive plant protein concentration (over 25g protein from soya alone) with low fat.
instructions: Boil soya chunks in water with a pinch of salt for 5 mins, rinse and squeeze out excess water.
Sauté onion, garlic, tomatoes, and spices in 1 tsp oil, then add green peas and soya chunks.
Add 1 cup water and simmer for 10 minutes until flavors blend thoroughly.
Serve hot with warm multigrain rotis and cooling salad.
